message.content:
Hipparchus is **not known for one single certain invention**; the safest answer is that he **helped found trigonometry** and **likely invented or improved several astronomical instruments**.[5][6][7]

The things most often credited to him are:

- **Trigonometry**: he compiled an early table of chords, which is why many historians call him the founder of trigonometry.[5][6][7][9]
- **Astronomical instruments**: sources credit him with inventing or improving devices such as the **astrolabe** or **astrolabion**, the **armillary sphere**, and other sighting instruments.[2][3][7][8]
- **Celestial mapping**: he created the **first known comprehensive star catalog** in the western world and made major advances in measuring the heavens, though this is more an achievement than an “invention.”[2][3][5]
- **Geometric/astronomical methods**: he pioneered the use of mathematical models for astronomy and is associated with early use of **geometric models** and **spherical trigonometry**.[3][6][7]

Some sources also say he may have had a role in the **Antikythera Mechanism** or the **stereographic projection**, but those attributions are less certain than his work on trigonometry and astronomical instruments.[1][2]

If you want, I can also give you a **short one-sentence answer** or a **list of his confirmed vs. disputed inventions**.
